facts.text: Yogi Rock was deployed at Ares Vallis during Mars Pathfinder in 1997.

Yogi was a large rock near the Pathfinder landing site, about one metre tall. Sojourner spent several sols driving to and analysing Yogi. APXS measurements showed it had a basaltic composition, different from Barnacle Bill, indicating variety in the local geology. Wind-sculpted features on its surface showed evidence of aeolian erosion.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Showed a basaltic composition contrasting with nearby Barnacle Bill, proving geological diversity exists within metres on the Martian surface.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Ares Vallis.
Yogi remains at Ares Vallis, its wind-sculpted face slowly being reshaped by Martian dust storms over the decades.
